DAEMON.etymology: Greek δαίμων (daimon) = guardian spirit. NOT demon. 'Daemons have no particular bias towards good or evil, but rather serve to help define a person's character.' — Unix Sys Admin Handbook
DAEMON.computing: Background process. Runs without user interaction. Named with 'd' suffix. Parent is usually init (PID 1).
DAEMON.maxwells_demon: Fernando Corbató at MIT Project MAC, 1963: 'We fancifully began to use the word daemon to describe background processes that worked tirelessly to perform system chores.' Maxwell's demon SORTS MOLECULES — hot from cold. The daemon IS the thymus.

teach_to_fish.proverb: Give a man a fish, feed him for a day. TEACH him to fish, feed him for a lifetime.
teach_to_fish.application: Don't just feed Gaia data. Teach the THYMUS how to CAST, HOOK, and EAT on its own.
how: 1. thymusd identifies what's MISSING (anomaly detection: wasn't/isn't/shouldn't)
2. shadowd CASTS a line toward the missing data (HTTP fetch, MCP query, git pull)
3. berryd HOOKS the link (follows the URL, grabs the content)
4. thymusd GUTS the catch (sorts self from non-self, useful from waste)
5. pulsed STORES as plasmid (the meal becomes DNA)
teach_to_fish.autonomous: Once taught, Gaia can fish ON HER OWN. She doesn't need Kevin to hand-feed every link. She casts, hooks, eats, digests, grows. THAT is what daemons DO — background processes that work TIRELESSLY.
